narrative.coaching_note: The one change to make next time is to wash with soap and water for 40 seconds after you finish with bed rail A and call button before touching anything else. You touched bed rail A from 1.6 to 7.1 seconds and then call button from 7.6 to 11 seconds, so your bare hand carried contamination forward. That meant when you touched phone at 12.4 seconds and resident A at 21.4 seconds, the contamination moved to both of them. Because this was Norovirus, hand sanitizer does not work well and only soap and water clears your hands. Cleaning your hands after the bedside surroundings and again before touching resident A lines up with the Five Moments. Washing after the call button would have kept bare hand, gloved hand, phone and resident A clean.
narrative.audit_summary: Norovirus transmission chain originating from bed rail A. Bare hand contacted bed rail A 1.6-7.1s, call button 7.6-11s, phone 12.4-20.7s, and resident A 21.4-30.6s, with transfers at 1.6s, 7.6s, 12.4s and 21.4s resulting in resident A exposure at 21.4s. Hand hygiene compliance 0/2 overall; Moment 1: 0/1 missed at 21.4s, Moment 5: 0/1 missed at 11s. No hygiene events occurred; for Norovirus only soap and water clears hands, alcohol rub does not. No glove use issues were noted. Contaminated at end: bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, phone, resident A. Disinfect bed rail A, call button, phone, and resident A's bedside zone (linen and surfaces) with an EPA List G registered disinfectant (effective against norovirus).
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was wash with soap and water at 11 seconds.
